definitions.explanation: The amount or proportion of sugar contained in food or drink. Also used loosely to refer to sugar or sweets in general, especially when talking about dietary intake.

examples.japanese: {糖分|とうぶん}を{控|ひか}えている。
この{飲|の}み{物|もの}は{糖分|とうぶん}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: This drink has a lot of sugar.

examples.japanese: {疲|つか}れた{時|とき}は{糖分|とうぶん}を{取|と}ると{頭|あたま}がすっきりする。
examples.english: When you're tired, taking in some sugar clears your head.

notes:
Compound of {糖|とう} (sugar) + {分|ぶん} (portion, content). Refers to sugar content in food and drink, or sugar intake in a dietary context.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {糖分|とうぶん}を{控|ひか}える: to cut back on sugar
- {糖分|とうぶん}を{取|と}る / {摂取|せっしゅ}する: to consume sugar
- {糖分|とうぶん}が{多|おお}い / {少|すく}ない: high/low in sugar
- {糖分|とうぶん}{補給|ほきゅう}: sugar replenishment

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {砂糖|さとう}: sugar (the physical substance)
- {糖質|とうしつ}: carbohydrates/sugars (nutrition label term)
- {糖分|とうぶん}: sugar content (more general, dietary context)
- {甘|あま}いもの: sweets, sweet things (casual)

Phrases like {疲|つか}れたから{糖分|とうぶん}{補給|ほきゅう} ("I'm tired, time for some sugar") are common in everyday conversation as a light justification for eating sweets.
